title: Ochre
author: WhatHasKHANGotToSay
selftext:
Ochre is a voxel project I've been working on since 2021.

Originally started as a simple Minecraft clone, but I migrated it to Bevy a while back -- then abandoned it for a while and came back with Claude Code and a renewed interest.

It's open-sourced, available on GitHub: [https://github.com/rornic/ochre](https://github.com/rornic/ochre)

Turns out the fact Bevy is driven entirely by code is a huge boon for building games using coding harnesses. 

Some cool features I've built:

* Terrain streams in around the player and falls back to coarser LOD meshes with a cross-fade, so the curved horizon reaches 16 km at the default render distance.
* 64 km x 64 km world. Droplet erosion carves valleys, hydrology routes rivers to lakes and the sea, and a climate pass sets temperature and moisture.
* A day and night cycle with sun, moon and stars, atmospheric scattering, volumetric clouds and weather including rain.

And AI gamedev tips from my own experience:

* For fast prototyping, generate a ComfyUI workflow with some specialised LoRA models to get quick textures. Example: [https://github.com/rornic/ochre/tree/main/.claude/skills/block-textures](https://github.com/rornic/ochre/tree/main/.claude/skills/block-textures)
* Build yourself a profiling skill so you can automatically A/B test new features and avoid performance regressions.
